items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: And some of the guys, Todd Williams and some of the other saxophonists had been working with Wynton.

ctx.x: The Thelonious Monk competition, when you came in second place one year I guess, did that do anything for you ostensibly? Open any doors for you or —

It made it so that people who had never heard of me before had now heard of me. So I guess that did something for me. I think I got one gig directly related to that. So in terms of work, not really. And I don’t think it got me any record deals or anything like that. There were no record companies climbing around me. They’re all climbing around number one. Number two and the rest were out pretty much, we’re on our own. But we © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

all, not me so much, but many of the other guys already had been working with people. They were already pretty high profile professional guys. I think the prerequisite, or one of the prerequisites to be in the competition was that you did not have a leader recording released on a major label. But there was no prerequisite, you know, you can’t have worked with a jazz legend. Because these guys certainly had.
